Hi Kyle — thanks for laying this out. Short answers up front, then recommended configuration and next steps.

Short answers:
- DNS: You can keep split-horizon. We recommend internal resolution for internal-only domains and conditional forwarding for public FQDNs used by Redwood. Redwood will accept TLS-backed connections by hostname; IP allowlisting is supported but we prefer FQDN+TLS for certificate validation.
- Egress destinations: We operate a small, documented set of control-plane endpoints and a separate set for model artifact fetching. For strict policies, use deterministic NATs (static egress IPs) and allowlist the documented IP ranges + hostnames.

Recommended configuration (practical):
1) Segmented egress channels:
   - Control plane (management/telemetry): outbound TCP 443 to api.redwood-inference.com and telemetry.redwood-inference.com (TLS/mTLS optional for sensitive telemetry). Use a dedicated NAT gateway with reserved static IPs.
   - Model fetching (runtime): allow outbound to model-storage.redwood-inference.com and the object-store endpoints (S3-compatible) listed in the safelist matrix. These should be on a separate NAT pool/route table to be auditable.
   - Third-party integrations: require explicit firewall rules per integration. Default is deny. If you plan to enable a vendor (eg, Datadog), request the vendor IPs/FQDNs and we will provide the required hostnames we call out for webhook callbacks, if any.
2) DNS handling:
   - Keep internal resolver as primary. Add conditional forwarders for *.redwood-inference.com to your outbound resolver or to a Redwood-managed DNS forwarder if you want central control. Avoid hardcoding IPs for service endpoints — prefer FQDN allowlist plus TLS validation.
3) Firewall rule examples (high level):
   - Allow: OUT tcp 443 -> api.redwood-inference.com (resolve to FQDN)
   - Allow: OUT tcp 443 -> model-storage.redwood-inference.com
   - Allow: OUT udp 123 -> time.redwood-inference.com (NTP)
   - Deny: ALL other outbound to internet unless explicit rule present

Attachments I included: safelist_matrix_v1.xlsx (mapping of hostnames -> purpose -> required ports) and egress-flow-diagram.vsdx. They contain the authoritative lists and a proposed NAT mapping.

Next steps:
- I'll kick off a short design call with Olga (networking) and Laura (solutions) to validate the NAT mapping and any procurement steps for static IPs.
- If you can share your procurement timeline for static IPs we can align – procurement lead time can affect rollout.

On the call — we can also show a fallback plan: if you cannot allocate static IPs immediately, use TLS+FQDN allowlisting with egress gateway proxy that performs SNI-based routing and mTLS where possible.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Forwarding a couple technical clarifications from the infra side — pasted below is a snippet we use when handing off an allowlist to customer firewall teams.

On Mon, Apr 18, 2027 at 10:02 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short answers:
> - DNS: You can keep split-horizon. We recommend internal resolution for internal-only domains and conditional forwarding for public FQDNs used by Redwood.

My additions:
- Deterministic NATs: we strongly prefer customers allocate a small NAT pool (2–4 IPs per AZ) mapped to specific route tables. That allows simple iptables/ACL rules and audit logs.
- TLS+SNI fallback: if you can't commit to static IPs immediately, use a managed egress proxy with outbound SNI inspection + mTLS for control-plane traffic. The proxy will present a fixed TLS session to the destination and allow using hostnames to permit connections.
- Example firewall snippet (pseudo-ACL):
  # Control plane (management)
  allow tcp 443 from 10.32.0.0/16 to <NAT_IP_POOL_CONTROL> dst-port 443 comment "redwood control plane via NAT"
  allow tcp 443 from 10.32.0.0/16 to model-storage.redwood-inference.com dst-port 443 comment "model pulls"
  # CRL/OCSP and time services
  allow udp 123 from 10.32.0.0/16 to time.redwood-inference.com
  allow tcp 443 from 10.32.0.0/16 to crl.redwood-inference.com

I attached a compact checklist we hand to customers when they finalize firewall changes. If you're on the call tomorrow, I'll bring a slide that maps our endpoints to required egress IPs and show how to pin those to your NAT pool.

-Olga
Olga Petrov
Principal Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
